interpretation: The sweep found no configuration that beats EXP-WS-SEQ-001's N1 with a CI excluding zero: the selected G03 (history length 64, base tokens) ensemble is -0.00019 NLL vs the N1 ensemble before calibration and -0.00030 [-0.00073, +0.00013] after (SEL-N1), i.e. within noise, while its advantage over the tree P is unchanged (-0.0039, CI below zero). The seed-0 SELECT lead of L=64 did not persist in seeds 1-2, which land at the SEQ-001 level; so the L=32 -> 64 change is not an improvement one can rely on. The richer prior-pitch tokens (Statcast zone, velocity and movement buckets of EARLIER pitches) and the batter-side context did not lower SELECT NLL in any of G04-G10 — the within-game sequence of pitch types and outcomes already carries the usable signal, and the extra physics tokens add noise at this data size. Deeper/wider encoders (d96 x 3) did not help either. Calibration repeats the CAL2 picture: CAL-CV selection lowers ensemble ECE from 0.0068 to 0.0052 with the CI touching zero; isotonic reaches 0.0026 but degrades NLL (+0.0006, CI above zero). Fan-display leaves stay well calibrated (whiff 0.001-0.003, ground ball <= 0.0014). Bottom line for the PM: the sequence-model gain over the tree is real on this exposed split (about -0.004 NLL) but saturated under this training recipe; further grid search is not worth GPU time; the next levers are (a) a prospective (unexposed) evaluation via the research shadow, and (b) if more modelling is wanted, a different recipe (longer training with lower LR / label smoothing / multi-game pitcher memory) rather than more tokens. LIMITS: EXPOSED DEVELOPMENT with many EVAL reads today; winner's curse on the selection; 3 seeds; CUDA runs reproduced SEQ-001 seed 0 bit-for-bit here but that is not a general guarantee; no adoption or winner claim.
